{"content":"## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Compatibility

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration that can run with the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) disabled. In that configuration, an application’s runtime choice also affects what happens when it imports extensions.

An extension must explicitly declare support for free threading. If it does not, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. How an extension makes the declaration depends on whether it uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

There is also a build detail for Windows: the compiler does not automatically receive the `Py_GIL_DISABLED` macro when building extensions. The configuration can be checked through `sysconfig`.

The support declaration is a compatibility signal that affects import behavior; it is not proof that the extension’s code is thread-safe. Extension authors therefore have a distinct compatibility responsibility when supporting CPython 3.13’s experimental free-threading configuration."}
